The compute strategy then layers MPI across ranks for the z-slabs with each rank driving its own GPU, likely using OpenMP or CUDA kernels for the per-rank local work.\n\nSince the FNV hash must stay sequential for identical results, I'm leaning toward reserving OpenMP for host-side tasks like field initialization, halo packing/unpacking, and parallelizable validation reductions like min/max/NaN checks, while keeping the hash and final Kahan sum sequential on the root after gathering.\n\nFor output, gathering works cleanly since z-slabs are contiguous in memory, so MPI_Gatherv can pull each rank's slab directly without reshuffling. I also want to keep the original grid-size defaulting behavior (nz falling back to nx when zero) without over-engineering guards for degenerate inputs like zero or negative dimensions.\n\nFor performance, I'm designing an overlapped communication/compute scheme: stage boundary planes of the cold field into pinned host buffers, exchange them via MPI_Sendrecv, then copy into device ghost planes, followed by a mu kernel, another halo exchange for mu, then the update kernel and buffer swap. To overlap, I'll compute mu on interior planes on one CUDA stream while the halo exchange runs concurrently, then handle the boundary-plane mu kernel afterward once the ghost data arrives.\n\nThe same interior/boundary pattern applies to the update kernel using mu's ghost planes, which is a standard and effective overlap approach, though I need to handle edge cases where the local z-range is too small to have an interior. default, and matching that behavior bit-for-bit on GPU would require controlling contraction consistently with -ffp-contract=off on host and --fmad=false on nvcc, though this still won't guarantee the hash matches the original's FMA-contracted build.\n\nI should treat \"equivalent semantics\" as acceptable within floating-point rounding rather than requiring a bit-exact hash match, and plan to build the original reference implementation in a scratch tmp directory first, run it to capture baseline output, then test the GPU version with and without FMA to see which aligns.\n\nNow I'm turning to the GPU kernel design: figuring out grid sizes (likely 256³ or 512³, with memory split across ranks), how to flatten 3D thread indexing into block/grid dimensions, and mapping local cell indices back to x/y/z coordinates.\n\nFor the mu kernel, I'm designing ghost-plane handling — storing extra planes above and below the local z-range so the Laplacian stencil can safely read neighbors, and working out how to clamp or replicate values at true global boundaries versus real inter-rank ghost exchanges.\n\nNow I'm moving to the halo exchange logic for the concentration field, thinking through which owned boundary planes need to be staged and copied between devices before the next kernel pass.\n\nI realize I can order things simply: launch the interior kernel on the compute stream first, then run the halo exchange on the host using the copy stream, sync that stream, and only then queue the boundary kernels on compute stream—no explicit events needed since they're naturally ordered after the completed copies. Though now I'm second-guessing whether the device-to-host copy of the boundary planes needs special handling too.\n\nI also need to handle the edge cases where nzl is 1 or 2 planes—when nzl==1 the single plane needs both ghosts with an empty interior, and when nzl==2 the interior is also empty with both planes acting as boundaries, so I should define interior as a range that can safely be empty. The ghost planes are only needed for boundary kernels at the two edge planes, and for genuinely global boundaries with no neighbor, no exchange is required since nothing reads that ghost. There's still an ordering subtlety: the device-to-host copy of the planes being sent needs to wait on the previous step's update kernel that wrote those values.\n\nTo keep ordering correct, I could just synchronize the compute stream at the start of each halo exchange so the copy stream always sees freshly written cold values before copying out, then do the MPI exchange and host-to-device copy back on the copy stream, synchronizing before launching the next kernel. The downside is that this approach sacrifices overlap between communication and interior computation, since the mu kernel would then need to wait until after the exchange completes rather than running its interior portion concurrently.\n\nSince mu boundary planes need cold ghosts, the cold exchange has to happen first. So the real order is: launch mu interior on compute (no ghosts needed), run cold exchange on the host in parallel, then launch mu boundary planes on compute afterward, sync, d2h the mu boundary, exchange, and h2d the mu ghosts—while overlapping this with the interior update launch on compute.\n\nI need to be careful about stream behavior: using the default legacy stream would implicitly serialize copy and compute work, so I should create both streams with the non-blocking flag and use async memcpy with explicit syncs to get true overlap.\n\nThen after mu's boundary planes finish, interior update can run since it only needs owned mu planes which are already complete. Next comes exchanging mu's boundary planes via device-to-host, MPI, host-to-device, followed by the boundary update and finally swapping cold/cnew — making sure the cold planes being exchanged are the fully finalized values from the previous step's sync.\n\nAt z=0 the kernel reads only its own index so ghosts don't matter there either. The non-overlapping approach would also work but I'll go with this plan, and for host staging I just need pinned buffers via cudaMallocHost — four buffers sized for the xy-plane, reused across sends and receives.\n\nFor the halo exchange I'll use non-blocking Isend/Irecv (4 requests total, then Waitall) rather than Sendrecv, sending the lo plane down and hi plane up with distinct tags for each direction so neighbors receive them as the correct ghost layer.\n\nFor OpenMP, I'll parallelize host-side field initialization over z-slabs before uploading to device, and use it again for the NaN/min/max validation scan since that reduction is order-independent — though the Kahan summation in print_results stays sequential since it's order-dependent.\n\nFor multi-GPU assignment, I'll split local ranks per node with MPI_Comm_split_type and assign device = local rank mod device count before any CUDA calls, erroring out if no devices are found.\n\nFor timing and output, I'm keeping the same format as the original—barrier before timing, MPI_Wtime for measurement, and performance computed as grid updates per time—while the final gather uses MPI_Gatherv so root assembles the full concentration array from each rank's owned slab for printing.\n\nOne subtlety I need to handle is overflow: for very large grids, the total element count or per-rank byte counts could exceed what a 32-bit int can hold in MPI's count parameters, so I should use derived datatypes (like a contiguous type representing one XY plane) so the actual counts passed to MPI stay small (number of planes rather than raw doubles), keeping things safe for huge domains.\n\nFor the final gather and validation, I only need to assemble the full field on rank 0 when it's actually required for printing or validation, so I should skip that expensive gather otherwise, and make sure all status/result printing happens only on rank 0 to avoid duplicate output.\n\nExit codes need to be consistent across ranks, so I'll broadcast the validation result from root before returning, and ensure MPI_Finalize and cudaFree run cleanly before exit. For the per-rank initialization of concentration values, I need to keep the same global linear-index formula so each local slab gets identical values to the original single-process version, just computed from local-to-global coordinate offsets.\n\nI'm also weighing floating-point contraction (FMA) behavior between the CUDA kernel and the original GCC-compiled host code, since default compiler flags could cause subtle mismatches, so I'll test both configurations. For MPI initialization, I'm considering MPI_Init_thread with MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED since only the main thread will issue MPI calls.\n\nNow I'm drafting the CMake setup: a project combining CXX and CUDA languages, pulling in MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA toolkit, and linking everything into the executable. The tricky part is that if the main source file is compiled as CUDA, I need OpenMP's compiler flags to reach nvcc correctly rather than being passed through unchanged, since nvcc doesn't understand raw GCC flags like `-fopenmp` directly.\n\nI'll set CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES to native since CMake and nvcc 12.0 support auto-detection. I'm also worried nvcc 12.0 might reject GCC 13 as unsupported, so I may need the -allow-unsupported-compiler flag if that happens, and I'll route warning flags through -Xcompiler.\n\nI should build the original code first as a reference to verify correctness, then write the new implementation, tracking the work with a todo list and staging files in a temp directory for comparison.\n\n","time":{"start":1793077904533,"end":1793077949915},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I should compare the magnitude of divergence between the no-FMA and FMA hash variants to confirm it's small before settling on this approach.\n\nA nice property I can lean on: computing each cell identically regardless of rank or GPU count makes results self-consistent across decompositions, independent of the host compute path entirely. One option worth considering is disabling FMA contraction on both host and device builds so the new code matches the no-fma reference build exactly, giving deterministic IEEE-as-written semantics.\n\nBut I realize the grader likely compares against the original default build's hash, which does use FMA contraction, so matching the no-fma reference wouldn't line up. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793078072745,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01XyYXe5RSih3VApFhjr4shv","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","content":"// Cahn-Hilliard phase separation benchmark.\n//\n// Parallelization (hybrid, all three always used):\n//   * MPI:    1D slab decomposition along z across ranks. Each slab is contiguous\n//             in memory, so gathering the result is a single MPI_Gatherv. Each rank\n//             exchanges one ghost plane with each z-neighbour per field update.\n//   * CUDA:   each rank drives one GPU (rank mod device count on the node). The\n//             chemical potential and the update are stencil kernels. Interior\n//             planes are computed while the halo exchange runs on a second stream.\n//   * OpenMP: host-side field initialization and the result validation scan.\n//\n// Numerical semantics match the serial original: same stencil, same clamped\n// (Neumann-like) boundaries, same evaluation order per cell. Each cell is computed\n// by the same expression regardless of decomposition, so the result does not\n// depend on the number of ranks or GPUs.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        cudaError_t err__ = (call);                                                      \\\n        if (err__ != cudaSuccess) {                                                      \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,             \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err__));                                          \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\n#define CHECK_MPI(call)                                                                  \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        int err__ = (call);                                                              \\\n        if (err__ != MPI_SUCCESS) {                                                      \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"MPI error at %s:%d\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__);                 \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr int TAG_TO_LOWER = 0;  // message sent to the rank below (z - 1)\nconstexpr int TAG_TO_UPPER = 1;  // message sent to the rank above (z + 1)\n\n// Global problem geometry plus this rank's slab.\nstruct Grid {\n    size_t nx, ny, nz;  // global dimensions\n    size_t z0;          // global z index of the first owned plane\n    size_t nzl;         // number of owned planes\n};\n\nstruct Phys {\n    double dx2, dy2, dz2;\n    double gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB, D, dt;\n};\n\n// 3D index calculation (host)\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Device buffers hold nzl + 2 planes: plane 0 and plane nzl+1 are ghost planes,\n// owned plane zl is stored at buffer index zl + 1.\n\n// Laplacian with clamped boundaries, evaluated on a device buffer.\n// (p) is the buffer index of the plane, (pzp)/(pzn) the buffer indices of the\n// z-neighbours (equal to p at a global boundary, which clamps).\n__device__ __forceinline__ double laplacianDev(const double* __restrict__ f, const size_t x, const size_t y,\n                                               const size_t p, const size_t pzp, const size_t pzn,\n                                               const size_t nx, const size_t ny,\n                                               const double dx2, const double dy2, const double dz2) {\n    const size_t S = nx * ny;\n    const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n\n    const size_t rowC = p * S + y * nx;\n    const double cc = f[rowC + x];\n    const double cxx = (f[rowC + xp] + f[rowC + xn] - 2.0 * cc) / dx2;\n    const double cyy = (f[p * S + yp * nx + x] + f[p * S + yn * nx + x] - 2.0 * cc) / dy2;\n    const double czz = (f[pzp * S + y * nx + x] + f[pzn * S + y * nx + x] - 2.0 * cc) / dz2;\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Chemical potential over owned planes [zlBegin, zlBegin + count).\n__global__ void chemicalPotentialKernel(const double* __restrict__ c, double* __restrict__ mu, const Grid g,\n                                        const Phys P, const size_t zlBegin, const size_t count) {\n    const size_t x = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t y = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (x >= g.nx || y >= g.ny) return;\n    const size_t S = g.nx * g.ny;\n    for (size_t k = blockIdx.z; k < count; k += gridDim.z) {\n        const size_t zl = zlBegin + k;\n        const size_t p = zl + 1;\n        const size_t gz = g.z0 + zl;\n        const size_t pzp = (gz < g.nz - 1) ? p + 1 : p;\n        const size_t pzn = (gz > 0) ? p - 1 : p;\n        const size_t idx = p * S + y * g.nx + x;\n        const double cv = c[idx];\n        mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * P.e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * P.e_BB - 2.0 * cv * P.e_AB)\n                  + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                  - P.gamma * laplacianDev(c, x, y, p, pzp, pzn, g.nx, g.ny, P.dx2, P.dy2, P.dz2);\n    }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update over owned planes [zlBegin, zlBegin + count).\n__global__ void updateKernel(const double* __restrict__ mu, const double* __restrict__ cold,\n                             double* __restrict__ cnew, const Grid g, const Phys P,\n                             const size_t zlBegin, const size_t count) {\n    const size_t x = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t y = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (x >= g.nx || y >= g.ny) return;\n    const size_t S = g.nx * g.ny;\n    for (size_t k = blockIdx.z; k < count; k += gridDim.z) {\n        const size_t zl = zlBegin + k;\n        const size_t p = zl + 1;\n        const size_t gz = g.z0 + zl;\n        const size_t pzp = (gz < g.nz - 1) ? p + 1 : p;\n        const size_t pzn = (gz > 0) ? p - 1 : p;\n        const size_t idx = p * S + y * g.nx + x;\n        cnew[idx] = cold[idx] + P.dt * P.D * laplacianDev(mu, x, y, p, pzp, pzn, g.nx, g.ny, P.dx2, P.dy2, P.dz2);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid launchChemicalPotential(const double* c, double* mu, const Grid& g, const Phys& P,\n                             size_t zlBegin, size_t count, cudaStream_t s) {\n    if (count == 0) return;\n    const dim3 block(32, 8, 1);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned>((g.nx + block.x - 1) / block.x),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>((g.ny + block.y - 1) / block.y),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>(std::min<size_t>(count, 65535)));\n    chemicalPotentialKernel<<<grid, block, 0, s>>>(c, mu, g, P, zlBegin, count);\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\nvoid launchUpdate(const double* mu, const double* cold, double* cnew, const Grid& g, const Phys& P,\n                  size_t zlBegin, size_t count, cudaStream_t s) {\n    if (count == 0) return;\n    const dim3 block(32, 8, 1);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned>((g.nx + block.x - 1) / block.x),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>((g.ny + block.y - 1) / block.y),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>(std::min<size_t>(count, 65535)));\n    updateKernel<<<grid, block, 0, s>>>(mu, cold, cnew, g, P, zlBegin, count);\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\n// Pinned host staging buffers for ghost-plane exchange.\nstruct HaloBuffers {\n    double* sendLo = nullptr;\n    double* sendHi = nullptr;\n    double* recvLo = nullptr;\n    double* recvHi = nullptr;\n};\n\n// Exchanges the boundary planes of a device field with the z-neighbours.\n// Global boundaries are not exchanged; the kernels clamp there instead.\n// Synchronizes the copy stream before returning; the compute stream is not touched.\nvoid exchangeHalo(double* dev, const Grid& g, size_t S, int rank, int size, MPI_Comm comm,\n                  MPI_Datatype planeType, cudaStream_t copyStream, const HaloBuffers& hb) {\n    const bool hasLower = rank > 0;\n    const bool hasUpper = rank < size - 1;\n    const size_t planeBytes = S * sizeof(double);\n\n    if (hasLower) CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(hb.sendLo, dev + S * 1, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, copyStream));\n    if (hasUpper) CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(hb.sendHi, dev + S * g.nzl, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, copyStream));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(copyStream));\n\n    MPI_Request reqs[4];\n    int n = 0;\n    if (hasLower) {\n        CHECK_MPI(MPI_Irecv(hb.recvLo, 1, planeType, rank - 1, TAG_TO_UPPER, comm, &reqs[n++]));\n        CHECK_MPI(MPI_Isend(hb.sendLo, 1, planeType, rank - 1, TAG_TO_LOWER, comm, &reqs[n++]));\n    }\n    if (hasUpper) {\n        CHECK_MPI(MPI_Irecv(hb.recvHi, 1, planeType, rank + 1, TAG_TO_LOWER, comm, &reqs[n++]));\n        CHECK_MPI(MPI_Isend(hb.sendHi, 1, planeType, rank + 1, TAG_TO_UPPER, comm, &reqs[n++]));\n    }\n    CHECK_MPI(MPI_Waitall(n, reqs, MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE));\n\n    if (hasLower) CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(dev + 0, hb.recvLo, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, copyStream));\n    if (hasUpper) CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(dev + S * (g.nzl + 1), hb.recvHi, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, copyStream));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(copyStream));\n}\n\n// Initial concentration on owned planes. Uses the global linear index, so the\n// field is identical for any decomposition. Host work parallelized with OpenMP.\nvoid initializeConcentration(std::vector<double>& c, const Grid& g) {\n    const size_t nx = g.nx, ny = g.ny;\n    const size_t S = nx * ny;\n    const size_t vol = g.nx * g.ny * g.nz;\n    const long long nzl = static_cast<long long>(g.nzl);\n    const long long nyl = static_cast<long long>(ny);\n\n#pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (long long zl = 0; zl < nzl; ++zl) {\n        for (long long y = 0; y < nyl; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t local = static_cast<size_t>(zl) * S + static_cast<size_t>(y) * nx + x;\n                const size_t linear_id = (g.z0 + static_cast<size_t>(zl)) * S + static_cast<size_t>(y) * nx + x;\n                // Pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[local] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Validation on the full (gathered) field. Scan parallelized with OpenMP.\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c) {\n    const long long n = static_cast<long long>(c.size());\n\n    bool bad = false;\n#pragma omp parallel for reduction(|| : bad)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        bad = bad || std::isnan(c[i]) || std::isinf(c[i]);\n    }\n    if (bad) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n#pragma omp parallel for reduction(min : minVal) reduction(max : maxVal)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, c[i]);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, c[i]);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n\n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of time steps (default: 20)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n[[noreturn]] void fatal(const char* msg) {\n    fprintf(stderr, \"%s\\n\", msg);\n    MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    std::abort();  // not reached\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = 0;\n    CHECK_MPI(MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided));\n\n    int worldRank = 0, worldSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &worldRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &worldSize);\n    const bool isRoot = (worldRank == 0);\n\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on all ranks)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (isRoot) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (isRoot) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n\n    if (nx == 0 || ny == 0 || nz == 0) {\n        if (isRoot) printf(\"Grid dimensions must be positive\\n\");\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793078112232,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bc89667001j0l9dpd5eXw9kJ","messageID":"msg_17bc8914a001Bs2s6Rz52wqLqP","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"That's odd - CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES set to \"native\" resolved to compute_52, which seems wrong since nvcc 12.0 may not properly support native detection, falling back to an old default. {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793078179577,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bc9b6f30016DNtzzJEBFu7NU","messageID":"msg_17bc9b19c0012WWKevjikZPNgs","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793078183243,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bc9b6f6001blogJdjRWg8oRp","messageID":"msg_17bc9b19c0012WWKevjikZPNgs","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"Trying to replicate GCC's exact vectorized contraction is too fragile, so I'll prioritize determinism over matching it exactly—disabling floating-point contraction to get bitwise identical results regardless of decomposition, since any performance difference is negligible.\n\nStrict IEEE semantics are the more defensible choice for matching the source as written, so I'll go with nvcc's `-fmad=false` and host `-ffp-contract=off`, setting these appropriately in CMake for CUDA and host compilation flags. The `-march=native` flag won't affect host math here since host code only handles initialization. Now I'm editing the CMake configuration accordingly.\n\n","time":{"start":1793078179574,"end":1793078183227},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793078183656,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bc9c53e0015kOnfAH59uzxs1","messageID":"msg_17bc9b19c0012WWKevjikZPNgs","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"text","text":"Reproducing GCC's exact FMA placement would mean matching its vectorized instruction selection, which is fragile and not worth it. I'll ship with contraction disabled on both host and device, which gives the source's IEEE semantics and makes results bitwise identical across any rank/GPU count. This matches the no-FMA reference exactly, and I'll document that the default-flags original differs in the last ulps.","time":{"start":1793078183230,"end":1793078183594}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793078313465,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bcbb3460014HwUdkiwwj1eEz","messageID":"msg_17bcbae39001WWZ0IW4Oidu3ov","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm puzzled why np=4 hangs specifically at 128^3 but not 64^3 — wondering if it's a real deadlock in the halo exchange or just slowness from GPU sharing, since with 4 ranks and only 3 GPUs, rank 3 would be doubling up on GPU 0.\n\nActually, I suspect it's an OpenMP oversubscription issue: each rank spawning 256 threads means 1024 total threads across 256 cores, and with busy-wait spinning under OMP_WAIT_POLICY this could thrash horribly rather than actually deadlock. I should test with OMP_NUM_THREADS reduced and a timeout to confirm.\n\n","time":{"start":1793078309702,"end":1793078313412},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793078313465,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bcbc1c6001IlENIPFG4vZ2Bd","messageID":"msg_17bcbae39001WWZ0IW4Oidu3ov","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"text","text":"Results match the reference hashes for every configuration tested so far. I'm walking through each step of the exchange sequence — the D2H copy, H2D copy, and boundary kernel launches — trying to find a point where a buffer could be read before it's fully synchronized, but each step seems to check out consistently so far.\n\nI realize the key safeguard is message ordering: since MPI preserves non-overtaking order between any pair of ranks, A's step-t mu send to B necessarily arrives before A's step-t+1 cold send, so B's posted mu-step-t receive matches correctly regardless of timing differences between ranks.\n\nI'm checking the buffer handling for A's Isend of the mu-step data — since the pinned sendHi buffer completes via Waitall before A proceeds, and the H2D copy from recvHi happens after its own Waitall, the matching logic seems sound. Still, I want to double check whether there could be distinct buffers causing a mismatch.\n\nLet me consider testing whether the bug lies in MPI itself by swapping the Isend/Irecv exchange for a blocking Sendrecv, or trying different BTL/PML configurations to rule out transport issues. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793080294265,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17be9b852001qhtHdmtzjUma5O","messageID":"msg_17be9b11b0017N5y6xjhb7BGDX","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm seeing large discrepancies across whole planes between ranks—differences of about 0.03 spanning entire 256-element planes, which suggests a ghost region or plane boundary issue rather than small numerical drift.\n\nTracing the dependency chain: since cnew at plane z depends on mu at z-1..z+1, and mu at z depends on cold at z-1..z+1, if cold at the boundary plane (plane 2, rank 1's first plane) is wrong, it would propagate to mu at planes 1-3 and then to cnew at planes 1-3—exactly matching the pattern of wrong planes I'm seeing. This points to a stale or incorrect cold value right at the rank boundary being the root cause.\n\nThis fits an MPI ghost-exchange bug where a received message is landing in the wrong buffer slot—either a ghost receive overwriting owned data, or rank 0 and rank 1 exchanging their boundary planes incorrectly—causing corrupted boundary values that then ripple outward through the stencil computation into the planes I'm seeing fail.\n\nI'm ruling out a race between the D2H copy and the Isend since there's already a stream sync in place, so I need to check whether the mu exchange's buffer reuse overlaps with the cold exchange's H2D copies, and look more carefully at the receive-side H2D copies in the exchange routine.\n\nEven though those also get synced, I'm wondering if the real issue is a send copy reading the device plane while a kernel on the compute stream is still writing to it. But since afterlaunch always calls a device sync after every kernel, that shouldn't be possible—so I need to double check that afterlaunch is actually serializing things the way I assume.\n\nAssuming it is, I'm shifting to suspect cross-process GPU sharing: when two ranks share the same physical GPU, their separate contexts get time-sliced rather than run concurrently, so a copy on one context shouldn't overlap a kernel on another—unless the copy engine itself behaves differently. I'm trying to test this by comparing runs where ranks share a GPU versus runs where each rank gets its own GPU, since the np=3/nz=6 one-rank-per-GPU case came back fully consistent, which points toward GPU sharing as the actual trigger.\n\nI notice in np=4, the sharing ranks (0 and 3) aren't adjacent neighbors, so they never directly exchange with each other—but in np=5, the sharing pairs (0,1) and (3,4) are exactly the rank pairs that communicate across the GPU0/GPU1 boundary, which lines up suspiciously well with where the corruption shows up.\n\nThis makes me suspect vader's shared-memory transport combined with pinned CUDA host memory—maybe single-copy mechanisms like CMA or process_vm_readv are misbehaving when reading from a sender's pinned buffer that's also registered with CUDA. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793081349153,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bf9f632001kkkU22AKHvFE7n","messageID":"msg_17bf9ef53001RL5cGvnL6QmRga","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"Since host-only MPI with a CUDA context showed no corruption, the issue must trace back to the D2H copies writing into host buffers before they're sent over MPI. I'm noticing that in cp.cpp the pageable async D2H copy behaves almost synchronously, yet we're still syncing explicitly, so the corruption in c.cpp seems tied specifically to that D2H copy pattern.\n\nTracing through the sequence carefully — host fills dir0 into dL, dir1 into dH, then D2H copies both into sL and sH, synced before Isend — everything looks correct, so sH should genuinely hold dir1 data that the receiver expects as rL. The fact that rL comes back as zero suggests either the receive never actually got matched to real data, or the sender's buffer wasn't populated yet at send time, possibly due to some mismatch in pinned vs pageable memory handling since both versions fail. I want to isolate whether the D2H-plus-sync step itself is producing correct results before the send happens.\n\n","time":{"start":1793081341490,"end":1793081349077},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793081386470,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bfa7a1300134yUPVy1Uvbl7m","messageID":"msg_17bfa7469001ybAtUdqH138qhn","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"Checking the PRE-SEND value at it0 ex1, sL0 comes out to 3, which matches the expected tag value for exercise 1 direction 0 — that's a correct match.\n\nBut sH0 shows up as 2, which is the tag for the previous exchange's direction 1, meaning it's stale. This points to a timing issue where the D2H copy for sH is reading stale device data — likely because the H2D copy populating dH on the legacy stream isn't properly synchronized with the async D2H readback happening on the non-blocking stream, so the ordering between them can't be guaranteed.\n\nSo sH0 ends up holding the stale dir1 value from ex0 instead of the updated dH content, which suggests the H2D write to dH at ex1 got lost or the D2H is reading an outdated snapshot. I'm trying to rule out whether a prior async copy or an MPI receive from the previous exchange could somehow be overwriting the sH buffer before I read it.\n\nSince rank 0 only uses sH for its upper neighbor and has no lower neighbor interaction, I can't find an obvious aliasing issue there. At this point it seems most productive to strip MPI out entirely and run a simplified single-process CUDA test replicating the same copy pattern, to see if the problem is really a CUDA runtime/driver issue rather than something in the MPI exchange logic.\n\n","time":{"start":1793081375251,"end":1793081386359},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793081386471,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bfaa57a001uq17yP8ZiaRoLl","messageID":"msg_17bfa7469001ybAtUdqH138qhn","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"text","text":"The check shows the sender's data is already wrong before `MPI_Isend`: the `sL` copy is correct but the `sH` copy still holds the previous exchange's values. That is a CUDA copy-ordering problem on the sender, not an MPI problem. I'll reproduce it without MPI, in a single process.","time":{"start":1793081386362,"end":1793081386371}}}

{"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793081395922,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bfacacd001qWacBHsvXslxJL","messageID":"msg_17bfac4ea0011sYfT5NdUk2f8N","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793081406155,"sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","part":{"id":"prt_17bfacad0001A3BvixTLhoJ5fA","messageID":"msg_17bfac4ea0011sYfT5NdUk2f8N","sessionID":"ses_e843aeb26ffe94FEnM47Ah57UF","type":"reasoning","text":"With a single process there's no problem, so the issue must be MPI-specific — maybe a prior Isend from the earlier exchange hasn't actually completed yet and is still referencing that same buffer, keeping it stale when the next exchange reads it.\n\nBut Waitall should guarantee completion and buffer freedom, so I'm wondering if the issue is instead in how CUDA-aware MPI handles the memory underneath — perhaps Open MPI's CUDA hooks or vader shared-memory transport are doing something unusual with the host buffer registration that causes a race rather than a legitimate completion. The pageable case also fails though, which argues against this being purely about pinned-memory DMA timing. I keep circling back to whether vader's single-copy mechanism for host-side sends might be leaving sH stale across exchanges for one of the ranks.\n\nI wonder if the H2D copy itself is reading stale host data, or whether Open MPI's CUDA-aware support is interposing on cudart calls in some way that corrupts memory during transfer. I should test disabling OMPI's CUDA support via MCA parameters like opal_cuda_support to see if that's what's interfering with the pinned memory registration.\n\n","time":{"start":1793081395920,"end":1793081406083},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

This points to the legacy stream's H2D copy interacting badly with other processes' streams when nothing forces a sync afterward.\n\nThis clicks into place: my initial cudaMemcpy H2D on the legacy stream isn't waited on by the non-blocking compute stream, so the first interior kernel and the copy-stream's halo exchange can read stale/zero data before that initial copy finishes. That explains why only step 0 corrupts, why a device-wide sync at entry masked it, and why the afterlaunch variant still fails since its sync comes too late relative to the very first interior kernel launch.\n\nThis explains why afterlaunch still fails with wrong mu values. But then entry-sync passing 12/12 is confusing, since mu interior at step 0 would also read stale data there — unless the race is timing-dependent, triggered only when GPU contention delays the legacy H2D copy. The real fix is to stop relying on legacy stream ordering entirely: route the init upload through cudaMemcpyAsync on the same stream used elsewhere so all operations share consistent stream semantics.\n\n","time":{"start":1793081540788,"end":1793081551796},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

In my program the initial upload uses `cudaMemcpy` (legacy stream), and the compute/copy streams are non-blocking, so nothing orders the first kernels and halo copies after that upload.
